metadata.summary: I'm well aware that we've only reached the halfway point of the 2026 season and so much can change in the NFL, especially at the back end of the year.
metadata.content: Jordan Love: Green Bay Packers quarterback is fearless and can lead Matt LaFleur's team to Super Bowl, says Neil Reynolds | NFL News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Jordan Love: Green Bay Packers quarterback is fearless and can lead Matt LaFleur's team to Super Bowl, says Neil Reynolds Sky Sports NFL's Neil Reynolds hails the form of Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers in his weekly column; the Packers improved to 6-3 on the year on Sunday with a dominant win over the New England Patriots to continue their march towards the NFL playoffs Neil Reynolds American Football Expert & Columnist Tuesday 10 November 2026 15:33, UK I'm well aware that we've only reached the halfway point of the 2026 season and so much can change in the NFL, especially at the back end of the year. But I'm now starting to believe the Green Bay Packers can make a serious run and they have emerged as true contenders in the NFC. Sunday's 45-27 win over the New England Patriots in Foxborough was a statement victory and it was a win that showed the Packers to be a complete team. Jordan Love is playing as well as any quarterback in the NFL this season and he backed it up on Sunday on a big stage in a game being called by Tom Brady as he threw for 372 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. messages.text: Ombudsman all set for Japan Cup swansong

metadata.summary: Having already cemented his status as a Godolphin great, Ombudsman will have the chance to end his stellar career on the global stage when tackling the Japan Cup later this month.
metadata.content: Ombudsman: Godolphin great set for Japan Cup swansong | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Ombudsman: Godolphin great set for Japan Cup swansong Champion Stakes hero Ombudsman is set for one final start in the Japan Cup before being retired to stud, trainer John Gosden has confirmed; The Godolphin-owned star, who is the back-to-back winner of the Prince Of Wales's Stakes, missed out on a trip to the Breeders' Cup last month. Tuesday 10 November 2026 14:01, UK Image: Ombudsman is set for a final start in the Japan Cup Having already cemented his status as a Godolphin great, Ombudsman will have the chance to end his stellar career on the global stage when tackling the Japan Cup later this month. Joint-trainers John and Thady Gosden elected against a Breeders' Cup run for the son of Night Of Thunder after his victory in the Champion Stakes, but he will now tackle a mile and a half for the first time in Tokyo on November 29 before stallion duties await at Darley's Kildangan Stud in Ireland in 2027. However, win, lose or draw in the Far East, Godolphin's managing director Hugh Anderson believes his legacy has already been secured and he will go down as "one of the best" to represent Sheikh Mohammed's operation on the racetrack. He told the Press Association: "John is a master trainer and has obviously got his eye very firmly on this prize. It's very exciting. messages.text: McTominay had heart 'shocked' two days before Scotland's World Cup opener

metadata.summary: Scott McTominay has revealed he needed to have his heart “shocked” two days before Scotland's World Cup opener against Haiti.
metadata.content: Scott McTominay: Scotland midfielder had heart 'shocked' two days before World Cup opener against Haiti | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Scott McTominay: Scotland midfielder had heart 'shocked' two days before World Cup opener against Haiti The 29-year-old missed Sebastien Pocognoli's first camp as he recovered from heart surgery; Scotland host North Macedonia on November 13, with their final Nations League game away to Switzerland three days later Tuesday 10 November 2026 17:54, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Scott McTominay reveals he needed to have his heart shocked before Scotland's World Cup opener against Haiti in the USA due to an irregular heartbeat, and says the tournament was the most disappointing time in his career Scott McTominay has revealed he needed to have his heart “shocked” two days before Scotland's World Cup opener against Haiti. The Napoli midfielder underwent a cardiac ablation procedure in Manchester in September to treat a mild, benign heart arrhythmia that first came to light after the Scots arrived in the United States in early June and then continued to affect him in August while back in Italy playing for his club. At the time, the Scotland camp, clearly keen to keep McTominay's situation under wraps, said the 29-year-old had missed training in the lead-up to the World Cup due to a stomach complaint. metadata.content: Sky backs Equal Sport Project's pledges to improve equality through five shared ambitions across industry | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sky backs Equal Sport Project's pledges to improve equality through five shared ambitions across industry Sky Sports is proud to support the Equal Sport Project, which is aiming to accelerate progress towards equality across sport through five shared ambitions; the project launches at a time when women’s sport is experiencing unprecedented momentum, yet significant inequalities remain Tuesday 10 November 2026 17:32, UK Image: Sky Sports is proud to support Equal Sport Project Sky Sports is proud to support Equal Sport Project, which aims to accelerate progress towards equality across sport through five shared ambitions. The Equal Sport Project unites sport in the UK behind five shared ambitions for women and men across sport - from local leisure centres to the biggest stadiums, and from grassroots pitches to boardrooms. Major sporting organisations from across the UK's sporting landscape - including the FA, RFU, Youth Sport Trust, England Netball, UK Sport, LTA, Women's Sport Trust, Women in Sport, Team GB and Sport England - have made specific pledges to drive progress and help turn these ambitions into reality. Brands and broadcasters are also playing their part, signalling growing support for the movement across the wider sporting industry.
